newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends down, mining sub-index up.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends down, mining sub-index up.

text.p: * Index ends a notch away from 3,300 point support
The Manila share index finished down on Tuesday as market activity remained centered on penny stocks, particularly mining issues, traders said.

"Speculative issues ruled the day and a steep drop in late trade was stopped as punters took profits on some speculative issues and switched to some blue chips," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
The main index fell by 8.41 points to 3,306.43.
Of the sub-indices, only the mining sector was up by 385.70 points, or 6.89 percent, closing at 5,983.59 points.
Volume of shares traded was heavy at 49.694 billion valued at 3.910 billion pesos. Decliners slightly outnumbered gainers 67 to 61 with 67 issues unchanged.
"We have been hovering at the support level and we will continue to consolidate," Harry Liu of Summit Securities said.
Traders said the market was unaffected by reports of the failing health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

Some investors were concerned about a political row triggered last weekend when a senior government official said the ruling party was in favour of amending the Constitution to enable President Fidel Ramos to run for a second term.
The move was fiercely denounced by opposition members.
"We are into a week-and-a-half of consolidation. I think this will still continue for the rest of the week before we resume an uptrend," said Diversified's Garcia.
